routes.description: Establish a necessary sustaining source of dependent being and show that classical divine attributes remain coherent with creation, temporality, freedom, evil, and revelation.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if dependent reality requires a divine ground and the principal coherence and evidential objections do not undermine identifying that ground with classical God.

motionBridge.description: Connect the necessary explanatory ground of dependent reality to the existence of the God affirmed by classical theism.

centralBridges.description: Show that changes from potency to act and essentially ordered causes require a presently sustaining foundational actuality.
Reconcile pure actuality with divine freedom, immutable knowledge, and creaturely temporal succession.
Explain divine goodness, creation, and permitted evil without treating God as one finite moral agent among others.
Explain why loving divine self-disclosure may be gradual and non-coercive despite nonbelief and religious disagreement.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Establish that natural reason can reach truths about God despite uneven access and intellectual difficulty.
Ground practical norms in the natures, ends, and flourishing of beings.

routes.description: Undermine classical theism by challenging its cosmological inference and identifying conflicts between its divine attributes and freedom, time, evil, and loving disclosure.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if the positive inference to classical God remains unsupported or if central divine attributes conflict with temporal reality, suffering, freedom, or widespread nonbelief.

motionBridge.description: Show that the evidence and coherence objections jointly favor denial of the classical-theist God specified by the motion.

centralBridges.description: Challenge termination, uniqueness, sustaining causation, and the inference from a first cause to the attributes of classical God.
Show that pure actuality and immutability conflict with alternative possibilities and knowledge of changing temporal truths.
Establish that apparently gratuitous evolutionary suffering is more expected without a perfectly good providential creator.
Show that perfect divine love is difficult to reconcile with nonresistant nonbelief and extensive religious disagreement.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Specify the simplicity, immutability, timelessness, impassibility, freedom, and goodness claims under examination.
Provide objective moral and epistemic grounds for moving from apparently needless suffering to an evidential objection.

sectionSelections.title: Dependence, Causal Series, and Sustaining Being
sectionSelections.rationale: This issue contains the principal positive inference from observed dependence to a foundational cause and the objections to termination and continuous sustaining causation.

proSelections.proposition: The first three Thomistic ways infer from motion, efficient causation, and contingency to a foundational cause sustaining essentially ordered causal reality.
Changes from potency to act cannot ultimately explain themselves and therefore require an actuality capable of grounding interconnected causal chains.

conSelections.proposition: The first three ways do not establish one common first cause for all causal series, and a beginningless essentially ordered series remains conceivable.
Created things may persist through existential inertia, so their continued existence does not evidently require concurrent divine actualization.

sectionSelections.title: Pure Actuality and Divine Freedom
sectionSelections.rationale: This issue determines whether the classical account of pure actuality can preserve the traditional claim that creation is a perfectly free divine act.

proSelections.proposition: Divine freedom consists in acting from an interior intellectual principle rather than merely possessing alternative possibilities, so fixed ends do not eliminate freedom.

conSelections.proposition: A purely actual God lacks unrealized possibilities and cannot do otherwise, contradicting traditional theism's claim that God is perfectly free.

sectionSelections.title: Eternity, Immutability, and Changing Knowledge
sectionSelections.rationale: This issue bears on whether an immutable and purely actual God can know a world whose temporally indexed truths and existing subjects change.

proSelections.proposition: God's eternal causative knowledge explains temporal changes in creatures without God passively learning new facts or undergoing intrinsic change.
God's eternity is a whole and simultaneous possession of being in which all temporal things are equally present and receive their being from God.

conSelections.proposition: Real temporal change requires God's knowledge to change, which conflicts with the immutability and pure actuality asserted by classical theism.
Causal knowledge does not resolve changing knowledge under presentism or growing-block theory because nonexistent past and future events cannot presently be caused.

sectionSelections.title: Evolutionary Evil and Divine Goodness
sectionSelections.rationale: This issue tests the evidential force of extensive animal suffering and the competing accounts of creation, moral evaluation, divine goodness, and permitted evil.

proSelections.proposition: The problem of evil must assess God as the transcendent universal cause who creates both actuality and potentiality, not as an ordinary maker working on antecedent material.
Divine nature is the metaphysical standard of goodness rather than an agent subject to a higher norm, while creatures owe worship to God as creator and final end.

conSelections.proposition: The profusion and apparently gratuitous distribution of evolutionary suffering is substantially more expected under philosophical atheism than under classical theism.
Soul-building and redemptive accounts do not explain hundreds of millions of years of suffering among nonhuman animals that are not moral agents.

sectionSelections.title: Divine Hiddenness, Revelation, and Religious Disagreement
sectionSelections.rationale: This issue addresses whether difficult access to belief and persistent religious diversity are compatible with a perfectly loving God seeking relationship with finite persons.

proSelections.proposition: God's existence is accessible to natural reason despite human limitations, while revelation makes that truth more broadly available.
Divine hiddenness is compatible with loving revelation because God addresses embodied and developing persons gradually and non-coercively through signs, inquiry, moral education, and mercy.

conSelections.proposition: Perfect divine love should keep every finite person able to enter a relationship with God, yet nonbelief prevents such relationship and creates a hiddenness problem.
The extensive disagreement among religious traditions is surprising under the hypothesis of a perfectly loving God.
